description:
Wire the TUI /tree dispatch to call Coder.get_tree/1 instead of Coder.get_entries/1,
so labels are visible in the tree overlay. Add TreeSelector.new_from_tree/2 to accept
pre-built tree nodes.

## Changes

### apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/components/tree_selector.ex

Add new_from_tree/2:
```elixir
@spec new_from_tree([TreeNode.t()], keyword()) :: t()
def new_from_tree(roots, opts \\ []) do
  # roots is already [TreeNode.t()] — no build_tree call needed
  leaf_id = Keyword.get(opts, :leaf_id)
  ...
  flat = Tree.flatten(roots, leaf_id)
  ...
end
```
This parallels new/2 but skips the build_tree/1 call since roots are already structured.

### apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/interactive.ex

Update dispatch_slash_command("tree") (around line 1856):
```elixir
defp dispatch_slash_command("tree", _args, state) do
  tree = Coder.get_tree(state.session)   # [TreeNode.t()] with labels resolved
  ts = TreeSelector.new_from_tree(tree,
    leaf_id: state.current_msg_id,
    max_visible_lines: max(5, div(state.height, 2))
  )
  focus(%{state | tree_selector: ts}, {:dialog, :tree_selector})
end
```
The max_visible_lines change also addresses opi-iu9.6 (windowed display height).

### Alias update
In tree_selector.ex (TUI), add:
  alias OctoPi.Coder.Session.TreeNode

The Tree alias already points to OctoPi.Coder.Components.TreeSelector.
Tree.flatten/2, Tree.filter/3, Tree.render_lines/2 all accept [TreeNode.t()] via FlatNode
which wraps TreeNode — no changes needed there since TreeNode is the same struct.

## Notes
- new/2 (takes [Entry.t()]) can remain for backward compat with tests that seed raw entries.
- The max_visible_lines wiring here also satisfies part of opi-iu9.6, but opi-iu9.6 still
  owns the render/2 windowing logic.

## Files
- apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/components/tree_selector.ex
- apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/interactive.ex

## Verification
Open /tree after labeling an entry (via a future opi-iu9.4 implementation, or by seeding a
label in the JSONL file). Confirm the label appears on the tree node.
